label: H.R. 8463

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Pre-Payment Fraud Prevention and Treasury Data Access Act aims to reduce improper payments and financial fraud involving federal funds. The bill establishes new pre-payment verification requirements for federal agencies, provides statutory authority and expands data resources for the Treasury's Do Not Pay system, allows state and local governments access to the system, and sets post-award reporting requirements for certain first-time federal award recipients.

affected_groups.effect: Must implement mandatory pre-payment verification procedures, apply fraud-risk indicators to programs, screen payees through the Do Not Pay system, and halt disbursements to noncompliant recipients.
Given access to the Do Not Pay system and required to screen persons or entities seeking federally funded program awards or payments against Do Not Pay data assets and risk tools.
Recipients of covered awards of $50,000 or more must submit a one-time report detailing the use of funds or face suspended disbursements.

key_provisions: Requires federal agencies to complete specific pre-certification checks—such as verifying funds availability, payee names, tax identification numbers, and active bank accounts—before directing the Treasury to issue a payment voucher.
Grants the Department of the Treasury statutory authority as the administrator of the Do Not Pay system and requires the inclusion of specified data assets and risk tools.

Mandates that executive agencies, state and local governments, and judicial/legislative branches screen payees and award applicants against appropriate Do Not Pay data assets and risk tools before making payments or awards.
Establishes penalties of up to a $250,000 fine, up to 5 years imprisonment, or both, for the unlawful disclosure of information obtained through the Do Not Pay system.
Requires first-time recipients of covered federal awards of $50,000 or more to submit a one-time post-award report on their use of funds within 180 days of receipt.
missing_information: The total estimated cost of implementing the new data systems and reporting requirements is not specified.
The exact timeline for when the final regulations or guidance will be fully promulgated by OMB and Treasury is dependent on future rulemakings within specified windows.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Pre-Payment Fraud Prevention and Treasury Data Access Act aims to reduce improper payments and financial fraud involving federal funds. The bill establishes new pre-payment verification requirements for federal agencies, provides statutory authority and expands data resources for the Treasury's Do Not Pay system, allows state and local governments access to the system, and sets post-award reporting requirements for certain first-time federal award recipients.
summary_detail.significance: This legislation places government-wide, standardized pre-payment controls across federal programs and broadens intergovernmental access to anti-fraud data systems. The requirements apply to executive agencies and participating state and local administrators handling federal funds, affecting federal disbursements, risk assessments, and reporting mandates for awards of $50,000 or more.
